note: The pantry. A shopping list built from these recipes should lift these out and set them aside, because you almost certainly already have them.
where the line is: A staple is bought once and spent by the spoonful: a tin, a bottle or a jar that outlives the recipe that sent you for it. Salt, pepper, oil, vinegar, baking soda, the ground spices.
Everything a recipe wants by the cup or the pound is shopping, however ordinary it is. Flour, butter, sugar, eggs, milk and rice are shopping. Salt is not.
Fresh is shopping, even when the dried version is a staple. Ground ginger is in here; fresh ginger is not. Dried thyme is in here; a sprig of thyme is not.
Universal, not cuisine-specific. Soy sauce and vinegar are in most kitchens; fish sauce, mirin, sesame oil and garam masala are things you buy for a cuisine, so they stay on the list.
One caveat a shopping list should honour anyway: a recipe that deep-fries wants a quart of oil, which is shopping no matter what this file says. If an amount is large, show it.
matching: Patterns are matched with matchesStaple() in src/lib/units.ts: a pattern hits when its words appear as consecutive whole words in the ingredient name. That is why "salt" does not claim "unsalted butter", and why "olive oil" does claim "extra-virgin olive oil". Plain substring matching gets both of those wrong. "except" is the short list of things a pattern would otherwise swallow — salt pork is pork. Read an entry as: matchesStaple(name, s.patterns) && !matchesStaple(name, s.except ?? []).
